raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
~~Add conditional logging prefixing based on `VLLM_ENABLE_PREFIX_PROC_LOGS` environment variable.~~

**Update:** per [@markmc's suggestion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/28582#issuecomment-3526137301) (see also #25700, #28666), this now uses an explicit `--log-prefix` / `--no-log-prefix` CLI argument and `ObservabilityConfig.log_prefix` config setting instead of an environment variable.

## Suggestion
Python's logging module already exposes `processName` as a standard LogRecord attribute `(%(processName)s)`, giving users full control over format without custom code. 

Separately: in enterprise environments, logs need to be parseable — no ANSI colors (breaks parsers/log aggregators), and a consistent format across all services.

__add_prefix works against both: it hardcodes format/color outside the standard Formatter pipeline, so users can't override or reposition it, and it likely forces colors even in non-TTY/production contexts.

**Basic example**: Companies using ELK stack, must update their parsers just for vLLM. 

I would recommend to deprecated this feature and instead encourage people to use logging format. 
- https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html#logging.LogRecord
- https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/examples/others/logging_configuration.html?h=logging


## Purpose
Allow full control over log format

## Test Plan

~~VLLM_ENABLE_PREFIX_PROC_LOGS=0 vllm serve [...]~~
`vllm serve [...] --no-log-prefix`

## Test Result
```bash
INFO:     127.0.0.6:56097 - "GET /health HTTP/1.1" 200 OK                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
# instead of
(APIServer pid=1) INFO:     127.0.0.6:56097 - "GET /health HTTP/1.1" 200 OK                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
# with processName
INFO:     127.0.0.6:56097 - MainProcess "GET /health HTTP/1.1" 200 OK                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
# Worker -> VllmWorker-0
# EngineCore_DP0 -> EngineCore_DP0
```

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a way to conditionally disable the prefixing of logs on stdout and stderr by using the `VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS` environment variable. This is a useful feature for environments where structured logging is important. However, the implementation has a critical flaw: the new environment variable `VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS` is used in `vllm/utils/system_utils.py` but is not defined in `vllm/envs.py`, which will cause a runtime `AttributeError`. I've added a comment with a suggestion on how to fix this. I've also suggested adding automated tests for this new functionality to prevent future regressions.

![critical](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/critical.svg)

This change introduces a dependency on `envs.VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS`, but this environment variable is not defined in `vllm/envs.py`. This will lead to an `AttributeError` at runtime when this code is executed.

To fix this, you need to add `VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS` to the `environment_variables` dictionary in `vllm/envs.py`. To maintain backward compatibility (prefixes enabled by default), you could define it like this:

```python
# In vllm/envs.py inside the environment_variables dict:
"VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS": lambda: bool(int(os.getenv("VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS", "1"))),
```

This will enable prefixes by default and allow users to disable them by setting `VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS=0`.

The environment variable `VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS` is not defined in `vllm/envs.py`. According to the pattern used in this codebase, you need to:

1. Add a type hint in the `TYPE_CHECKING` block (around line 13-226 in `vllm/envs.py`):
   ```python

   ```

2. Add the actual environment variable definition in the `environment_variables` dictionary (look for similar boolean flags around line 581-1410 in `vllm/envs.py`):
   ```python
   "VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS": lambda: bool(int(os.getenv("VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS", "1"))),
   ```

Note: The default value should be "1" (True) to maintain backward compatibility, as the current behavior is to always add prefixes.

The new environment variable `VLLM_ENABLE_PREFIX_PROC_LOGS` is defined in the TYPE_CHECKING block but is missing from the `environment_variables` dictionary. This means the environment variable won't actually be read from the environment and will always use the default value (`True`).

You need to add an entry to the `environment_variables` dictionary (around line 1487, after `VLLM_FLAT_LOGPROBS`) like:

```python
# Flag to enable/disable process log prefixing with process name and PID.
# When enabled (default), logs are prefixed with "(ProcessName pid=123)".
# When disabled, logs are not prefixed, allowing for custom log formatting.
"VLLM_ENABLE_PREFIX_PROC_LOGS": lambda: bool(int(os.getenv("VLLM_ENABLE_PREFIX_PROC_LOGS", "1"))),
```

This change introduces a dependency on `envs.VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS`, but this environment variable is not defined in `vllm/envs.py`. This will lead to an `AttributeError` at runtime when this code is executed.

To fix this, you need to add `VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS` to the `environment_variables` dictionary in `vllm/envs.py`. To maintain backward compatibility (prefixes enabled by default), you could define it like this:

```python
# In vllm/envs.py inside the environment_variables dict:
"VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS": lambda: bool(int(os.getenv("VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS", "1"))),
```

This will enable prefixes by default and allow users to disable them by setting `VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS=0`.

**<sub><sub>![P0 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P0-red?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accessing undefined env flag crashes log decoration**

The new `if envs.VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS:` branch references an environment value that is not declared in `vllm.envs.environment_variables`. Because `envs.__getattr__` raises `AttributeError` for unknown keys, any caller of `decorate_logs()` (e.g. API server startup or worker processes) will now fail before logging is configured. Unless `VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS` is added to `envs.py`, this change prevents the service from booting rather than simply skipping log prefixing.

The environment variable `VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS` is not defined in `vllm/envs.py`. According to the pattern used in this codebase, you need to:

1. Add a type hint in the `TYPE_CHECKING` block (around line 13-226 in `vllm/envs.py`):
   ```python
   VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS: bool = True
   ```

2. Add the actual environment variable definition in the `environment_variables` dictionary (look for similar boolean flags around line 581-1410 in `vllm/envs.py`):
   ```python
   "VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS": lambda: bool(int(os.getenv("VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS", "1"))),
   ```

Note: The default value should be "1" (True) to maintain backward compatibility, as the current behavior is to always add prefixes.

The new environment variable `VLLM_ENABLE_PREFIX_PROC_LOGS` is defined in the TYPE_CHECKING block but is missing from the `environment_variables` dictionary. This means the environment variable won't actually be read from the environment and will always use the default value (`True`).

You need to add an entry to the `environment_variables` dictionary (around line 1487, after `VLLM_FLAT_LOGPROBS`) like:

```python
# Flag to enable/disable process log prefixing with process name and PID.
# When enabled (default), logs are prefixed with "(ProcessName pid=123)".
# When disabled, logs are not prefixed, allowing for custom log formatting.
"VLLM_ENABLE_PREFIX_PROC_LOGS": lambda: bool(int(os.getenv("VLLM_ENABLE_PREFIX_PROC_LOGS", "1"))),
```
```suggestion

# ... (other code)

# Dictionary mapping environment variable names to their loader functions.
environment_variables = {
    # ... (other environment variables)
    "VLLM_FLAT_LOGPROBS": lambda: bool(int(os.getenv("VLLM_FLAT_LOGPROBS", "0"))),
    # Flag to enable/disable process log prefixing with process name and PID.
    # When enabled (default), logs are prefixed with "(ProcessName pid=123)".
    # When disabled, logs are not prefixed, allowing for custom log formatting.
    "VLLM_ENABLE_PREFIX_PROC_LOGS": lambda: bool(int(os.getenv("VLLM_ENABLE_PREFIX_PROC_LOGS", "1"))),
    # ... (other environment variables)
}
```

All other logging env vars (`VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL`, `VLLM_LOGGING_PREFIX`, `VLLM_LOGGING_STREAM`, `VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH`, `VLLM_LOGGING_COLOR`, `VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL`, etc.) are explicitly excluded from compile cache keys. Without this addition, changing this logging preference will unnecessarily invalidate the torch.compile cache.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a way to conditionally disable the prefixing of logs on stdout and stderr by using the `VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS` environment variable. This is a useful feature for environments where structured logging is important. However, the implementation has a critical flaw: the new environment variable `VLLM_PREFIX_LOGS` is used in `vllm/utils/system_utils.py` but is not defined in `vllm/envs.py`, which will cause a runtime `AttributeError`. I've added a comment with a suggestion on how to fix this. I've also suggested adding automated tests for this new functionality to prevent future regressions.
